The *Ekachattiyattheraapadāna* is a verse text in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The work recounts the past karmic deeds of the elder Ekachattiya. On SuttaCentral, translations of the text are recorded in five languages, although no curated parallels in external canonical collections are identified [SuttaCentral].
Textual reuse data generated by DharmaNexus highlights substantial internal repetition within Pali literature, identifying 125 matching passages shared across 42 other Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Most notably, a large section of the text (§1.1–9.4) shares an extended near-verbatim overlap (1,889 characters, 0.93 similarity) with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Dutiyo bhāgo), alongside additional matches in the first volume of the same commentary [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, recurring stock verses—chiefly clustered between segments 9.1 and 14.1—are shared with numerous other *Therāpadāna* poems, including the *Ekadīpiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 418), the *Ekāsanadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 425), and a homonymous poem, the *Ekachattiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 414) [DharmaNexus]. Automated cross-language alignments identify weak similarities with northern Buddhist texts, such as the Tibetan *Ārya-avalokana-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra* (D0195) and the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna*, though these represent machine alignments rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
